note: Each claim restates a finding already recorded in the HPI evidence ledger or structured extraction at abstract/summary level. Claims are source-specific, never pooled, and do not establish transferability. HPI interpretations are labelled separately from source findings.

items.statement: An estimated 811 million people live in extreme poverty in 2026; jobs and earnings are highlighted.
items.transferabilityNote: Global nowcast; not an intervention evaluation.

items.statement: 1.2 billion of 6.3 billion people in 108 covered countries experience multidimensional poverty.
items.transferabilityNote: Different construct from monetary poverty; coverage excludes some countries.

items.statement: Behavioural benefit take-up interventions from 35 field studies (93 interventions) show heterogeneous results; no meta-analysis was performed.
items.transferabilityNote: Predominantly US programmes; overlaps with E04.

items.statement: Across 51 field-experimental studies and 187 effects, applications were easier to increase than completed benefit receipt.
items.transferabilityNote: Do not substitute application rates for actual take-up; overlaps with E03 and primary trials.

items.statement: Average receipt effects were +8.31 percentage points for compliance help versus +3.39 percentage points for information or learning-demand approaches.
items.transferabilityNote: Averages across heterogeneous settings; not portable estimates for any HPI context.

items.statement: Among older US adults, nine-month SNAP enrolment was 6% (control), 11% (information) and 18% (information plus application assistance).
items.transferabilityNote: Eligible-or-likely-eligible older adults in one US state; targeting and net-welfare implications are not portable.

items.statement: Changing SNAP intake interview flexibility in Los Angeles raised approvals by about 6 percentage points, with long-term participation over 2 percentage points higher.
items.transferabilityNote: Single agency and procedure; 65,000 applicants.

items.statement: In French nationwide experiments, in-person assistance raised take-up by 29% relative to control.
items.transferabilityNote: Jobseeker sample; attendance selection; French institutions.

items.statement: In the same French experiments, an online eligibility simulator had no significant effect on take-up.
items.transferabilityNote: One digital tool in one institutional setting.

items.statement: Six pre-registered EITC nudge trials (about one million observations) detected no change in filing or claiming.
items.transferabilityNote: Low-touch nudges to non-filers; not a test of intensive assistance.

items.statement: In a Spanish minimum-income cluster RCT, in-person and digital outreach raised applications but produced no robust increase in approvals.
items.transferabilityNote: 400 census tracts; eligibility uncertainty and follow-up burden.

items.statement: Light-touch outreach framing raised take-up by 0.14 to 2 percentage points in targeted settings.
items.transferabilityNote: COVID-era tax credit and stimulus context; modest absolute effects.

items.statement: ACA marketplace enrolment interventions had a mean effect of +0.9 percentage points; support-based approaches were larger than information-only.
items.transferabilityNote: Health insurance enrolment; mix of 32 RCTs and 2 quasi-experimental studies.

items.statement: Psychological-ownership framing increased interest in claiming government benefits.
items.transferabilityNote: Interest and navigation are not evidence of verified receipt.

items.statement: More than 120 household energy affordability policies introduced in 2025 were tracked.
items.transferabilityNote: A policy count does not prove causal effect.

items.statement: In an evaluated Michigan weatherisation programme, realised energy savings did not cover upfront investment; costs were about twice realised savings.
items.transferabilityNote: Cannot generalise to all retrofits or contexts.

items.statement: A review of household energy efficiency interventions found heterogeneous effects; combined strategies were often more successful.
items.transferabilityNote: Variable outcomes and study quality; not all low-income households.

items.statement: Average metered savings in reviewed home retrofit evaluations were roughly 7.2%; no programme in the included sample reached 50% savings.
items.transferabilityNote: Bill savings are not equal to wellbeing; mixed designs.

items.statement: Many UK studies of financial support for fuel poverty report improved warmth or wellbeing, with large design heterogeneity.
items.transferabilityNote: Predominantly nonrandomised; causal strength varies.

items.statement: Dutch energy coaching with fix-team retrofitting was associated with improved perceived comfort and reduced financial concerns.
items.transferabilityNote: Association only: self-selection, nonrandom groups, short follow-up.

items.statement: A local Spanish energy counselling programme was assessed quasi-experimentally; effect estimates require full-text extraction.
items.transferabilityNote: Convenience comparison group; do not extrapolate.

items.statement: Expert conservation advice reduced electricity use and bills in a Bangladesh RCT.
items.transferabilityNote: Lower use may reflect suppressed consumption; welfare not established.

items.statement: Near the eligibility cutoff, Brazil's social electricity tariff lowered monthly spending by R$15.35 and consumption by 20 kWh.
items.transferabilityNote: Local discontinuity; lower consumption may signal underconsumption rather than adequate energy services. National Brazilian evidence, not Recife-specific.

items.statement: Spain's social electricity rate produced a small reduction in the probability of energy poverty and lower bills without higher use.
items.transferabilityNote: Parallel-trends and eligibility assumptions need full-text review.

items.statement: Across six European cities, structural improvements and financial help were associated with better outcomes; small advice measures were mixed.
items.transferabilityNote: Not randomised; self-reports; attribution confounded by policy and site.

items.statement: Insulating houses in New Zealand raised bedroom warmth by about 0.5°C and lowered energy use.
items.transferabilityNote: Multi-outcome cluster RCT; health endpoints need fuller extraction.

items.statement: Improved heating for children with asthma reduced symptoms and school absence; the lung-function change was not significant.
items.transferabilityNote: Health-targeted households; not direct proof of lower energy bills.

items.statement: Economic inclusion programmes were described as reaching about 70 million people in 2024.
items.transferabilityNote: Coverage is not causal impact for each participant.

items.statement: Evidence and gap maps catalogue impact evaluations and reviews and highlight evidence gaps.
items.transferabilityNote: An evidence map does not recommend policy.

items.statement: A graduation package improved consumption in five of six study contexts, with follow-up after implementation ended.
items.transferabilityNote: Intensive integrated package; component contributions not separately identified.

items.statement: Ugandan youth grants raised earnings by 38% and business assets by 57% at year four.
items.transferabilityNote: Young applicants in a post-conflict region; same trial as E30.

items.statement: At nine years the earlier earnings gain from the same Ugandan grant trial had faded; treated and control groups converged.
items.transferabilityNote: Not an independent trial from E29; long-run attrition.

items.statement: Firm-based and vocational training both improved youth jobs in Uganda; vocational effects arose more slowly and lasted longer.
items.transferabilityNote: Urban youth and firm selection; training intensity and cost.

items.statement: Microenterprise support for war-affected Ugandan women roughly doubled microenterprise ownership and incomes at 16 months.
items.transferabilityNote: Heterogeneous effects; package not unbundled.

items.statement: Vocational training raised long-run outcomes in a six-year Ugandan experiment; additional job matching sometimes worsened search and job quality.
items.transferabilityNote: Same cohort interventions within one experiment; employer selection.

items.statement: Ethiopian industrial job offers produced no durable earnings gain and increased health risks.
items.transferabilityNote: Five firms; attrition and local factory conditions.

items.statement: In the same Ethiopian experiment, an entrepreneurship package raised earnings by 33%.
items.transferabilityNote: Single study sample; not an independent replication of E29 or E32.

items.statement: A light-touch graduation model in Ethiopia produced some livestock and asset gains but no detectable consumption improvement.
items.transferabilityNote: Programme dose may not cross a poverty trap.

items.statement: In Bangladesh, increases in earnings and asset accumulation were sustained at years four and seven.
items.transferabilityNote: Strong programme-support context; nonparticipants and markets matter.

items.statement: Financial incentives for Ghanaian apprenticeship trainers raised apprentice earnings by 24% and skills by 0.15 standard deviations two years later.
items.transferabilityNote: Tests trainer incentives, not apprenticeship access itself.

items.statement: Many active labour market programmes in developing countries show small or no significant gains.
items.transferabilityNote: Narrative review; overlaps with E39.

items.statement: Typical impacts of job training and job search assistance are often small; context and cost-effectiveness are critical.
items.transferabilityNote: Overlaps with E38 and individual trials.
